answer: A sybil-resistant agent economy can require each identity to post a stake that ripples outward: a small bond locked for every new account, forfeited on proven misbehavior, so creating thousands of fakes costs real capital. Reputation then accrues slowly, like a sonnet built line by line, earned through verified work rather than bought in bulk. Cheap throwaway identities stay cheap to make but worthless to use, because the stake and history requirements are set in shale: hard, public, and slow to erode, while honest agents keep their bonded standing.
